subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or is the current foreground lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostic recovery the intended product behavior?
rationale: The source-backed issue remains, but the durable fix changes scheduler and session-state ordering guarantees for interactive turns versus context maintenance.

options.title: Isolate maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency or background lane so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for maintenance to finish.

options.title: Preempt foreground maintenance
options.body: Keep the session-lane model but make compaction and memoryFlush abortable and reschedulable when user messages arrive.

options.title: Accept mitigation only
options.body: Treat the 180-second timeout and stuck-session recovery as sufficient, leaving foreground turns blocked during active maintenance windows.

recommendation.title: Isolate maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency or background lane so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for maintenance to finish.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the open adjacent stuck-session recovery experiment and is the clearest listed person for the scheduling/recovery product decision.
